title: Party Barge Myths Houston Believes
why: Cold-audience pattern interrupt: knocks down the four objections that stop bookings (work, no waterfront, cost, who it's for).
hook_options: Four things Houston gets wrong about party barges.
You have heard these. They are wrong.
Myth: it's a workout. Fact: keep reading.
caption: Four things we hear every week about party barges, and the short honest answer to each. Clear Lake is closer than you think and a private boat costs about one bar tab. #HoustonPartyBarge #ClearLake #ThingsToDoInHouston #Kemah

slides.headline: Four things Houston gets wrong about party barges.
slides.body: We hear these every week. Here's the short version.

slides.headline: You'll be working the whole time.
slides.body: People picture a workout on water and pass.

slides.headline: The motor does the work.
slides.body: Fully motorized, captain at the wheel. You sit, sip, and point at Kemah.

slides.headline: Houston doesn't have a waterfront.
slides.body: Bayous, freeways, humidity. That's the reputation.

slides.headline: Clear Lake is 30 minutes from downtown.
slides.body: Seabrook, minutes past the Kemah Boardwalk. Open water that runs out to Galveston Bay.

slides.headline: A private boat costs a fortune.
slides.body: Sounds like yacht money, so groups never ask.

slides.headline: A whole boat costs about one bar tab.
slides.body: Private charters start around $800 for up to 26. A 20-person Houston bar tab runs $600 to $800.

slides.headline: It's only for bachelorettes.
slides.body: Bachelorettes love it. They're not the only ones on board.

slides.headline: Birthdays, teams, family in town.
slides.body: Ages 8 and up, no dress code. Birthday crowns and work polos both make the boat.

slides.headline: Myths busted. Book the real thing.
slides.body: Public cruises and private charters out of Seabrook. houstonpedalbarge.com
